"'''Fast Car'''" is a song by American singer-songwriter [[Tracy Chapman]], released as her debut single on April 6, 1988, by [[Elektra Records]]. It served as the [[lead single]] from her 1988 [[Tracy Chapman (album)|self-titled debut studio album]]. Chapman's appearance at the [[Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute]] concert in June 1988 helped the song become a top-ten hit in the United States, reaching number six on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and led the album to top the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. The single also reached number five on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and topped the charts of five other countries.

"Fast Car" received three nominations at the [[31st Annual Grammy Awards]] in 1989: [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]], [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]], and [[Grammy Award for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance|Best Female Pop Vocal Performance]], the last of which it won. It also received an [[MTV Video Music Award]] nomination for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Female Video|Best Female Video]].

Since the release of Chapman's original, the song has had success in two electronic dance versions by Swedish DJ Tobtok and British DJ [[Jonas Blue]], as well as a [[country music|country]] cover by American singer [[Luke Combs]]. Combs's version was a number-one single on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Country Songs]] and [[Country Airplay]] charts in 2023, and won Chapman the [[Country Music Association Awards|Country Music Association Award]] for [[Country Music Association Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]], making her the first black person to win the award.

"Fast Car" is a song by American singer-songwriter Tracy Chapman, released as her debut single on April 6, 1988, by Elektra Records. It served as the lead single from her 1988 self-titled debut studio album. Chapman's appearance at the Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute concert in June 1988 helped the song become a top-ten hit in the United States, reaching number six on the Billboard Hot 100 and led the album to top the Billboard 200. The single also reached number five on the UK Singles Chart and topped the charts of five other countries.

"Fast Car" received three nominations at the 31st Annual Grammy Awards in 1989: Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Best Female Pop Vocal Performance, the last of which it won. It also received an MTV Video Music Award nomination for Best Female Video.

Since the release of Chapman's original, the song has had success in two electronic dance versions by Swedish DJ Tobtok and British DJ Jonas Blue, as well as a country cover by American singer Luke Combs. Combs's version was a number-one single on the Billboard Hot Country Songs and Country Airplay charts in 2023, and won Chapman the Country Music Association Award for Song of the Year, making her the first black person to win the award.

sections.heading: Music and lyrics
sections.wikitext:
According to ''[[Metro Weekly]]'' critic Chris Gerard, "Fast Car" tells the story of a working woman trying to escape the [[cycle of poverty]], set to "glowing [[folk rock]]". In a 2010 interview, Chapman explained that the song wasn't "directly autobiographical," but rather "very generally represents the world that I saw it when I was growing up in Cleveland, Ohio, coming from a working class background."{{Cite web |title=BBC World Service - News - Striking a Chord: songs that speak to a generation, country or culture |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/worldservice/news/2010/08/100810_striking_a_chord_sl.shtml |access-date=March 29, 2025 |website=www.bbc.co.uk |language=en-GB}}
I’ve been raised by a single mom, I was just watching people, being in a community of people who were struggling. So everyone was really just, one, working hard, two, hoping that things would get better. In part everything that a person writes is autobiographical but the songs are directly so, and most of them were not and Fast Car wasn't one that was directly autobiographical. I never had a Fast Car, it’s just a story about a couple, how they are trying to make a life together and they face challenges.
The song's arrangement was described by ''[[Orlando Sentinel]]'' writer Thom Duffy as "subtle folk-rock", while ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine's Gary Trust deemed the record a "[[Folk-pop|folk/pop]]" song. Critic [[Dave Marsh]] called it an "optimistic folk-rock narrative" about characters living in a [[homeless shelter]].

sections.text:
Elektra Records released "Fast Car" as a single on April 6, 1988, one day after the album Tracy Chapman. That June, Chapman appeared at the Nelson Mandela 70th Birthday Tribute concert, where she was scheduled to sing three songs. Just before surprise guest Stevie Wonder walked onstage, he learned that his keyboard's floppy disk had gone missing. He left in a panic, forcing the event organizers to usher Chapman back to the stage with nothing but a microphone and her guitar. As the organizers readied the stage for the following act, Chapman performed "Fast Car" and "Across the Lines". This performance brought widespread attention to her music, with sales for Tracy Chapman increasing enough for it to top the Billboard 200 chart on August 27, 1988. "Fast Car" itself would reach number six on the Billboard Hot 100 the same week.

A remastered recording of "Fast Car" was issued by Elektra in 2015. The song reached one billion streams on Spotify on January 17, 2025.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: John Tague from ''[[New Musical Express|NME]]'' wrote, "'Fast Car' is a typically well expressed lament, not for those who have suffered extraordinary circumstances, but for those who escape one form of dead end existence only to fall into another, relative material success without the consolation of dreams for the future. It's a keenly felt depiction of the impossibility of escape, rendered tastefully and gracefully, charming in its simplicity."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=John|last=Tague|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/51010780433/|title=Singles|magazine=[[New Musical Express|NME]]|date=May 28, 1988|page=16|access-date=October 30, 2023}}</ref> ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked "Fast Car" number 167 on their 2004 list of the [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|500 Greatest Songs of All Time]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=December 9, 2004 |title=The RS 500 Greatest Songs of All Time |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/500songs/page/2 |url-status=dead |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060820114448/http://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/500songs/page/2 |archive-date=August 20, 2006 |access-date=January 15, 2010}}</ref> It was Chapman's only song on the list, and the highest-ranking song performed and written solely by a female artist. When ''Rolling Stone'' updated the list in 2021, "Fast Car" was promoted to number 71.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=September 15, 2021 |title=The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-songs-of-all-time-1224767/tracy-chapman-fast-car-3-1225267/ |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US |access-date=May 30, 2023}}</ref> ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' named it the 86th-best song of the 1980s in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2015 |title=The 200 Best Songs of the 1980s |url=http://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/9700-the-200-best-songs-of-the-1980s/?page=6 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160614150330/http://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/9700-the-200-best-songs-of-the-1980s/?page=6 |archive-date=June 14, 2016 |website=Pitchfork}}</ref> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine ranked "Fast Car" number 15 in their list of "The 100 Greatest [[LGBTQ+]] Anthems of All Time" in 2025.<ref>{{cite magazine|first1=Joe|last1=Lynch|first2=Stephen|last2=Daw|first3=Hannah|last3=Dailey|first4=Glenn|last4=Rowley|first5=Hannah|last5=Jocelyn|first6=Lucas|last6=Villa|url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/lgbtq-anthems-queer-pride-songs/|title=The 100 Greatest LGBTQ+ Anthems of All Time|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=June 4, 2025|access-date=June 20, 2025}}</ref> In June 2026, [[CBS News]] included the song in its list of the 250 essential American songs of the past 250 years, one of two Chapman songs to make the list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Essential American Songbook |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/projects/2026/sunmo-american-songbook/ |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en}}</ref>

The single was certified quintuple platinum in the United Kingdom by the British Phonographic Industry (BPI) in 2026, based on downloads and streaming. By 2016, it had sold 661,500 copies in the United Kingdom.

Tobtok's version was published on SoundCloud on October 30, 2015, and released commercially on November 27, 2015, through Good Soldier Records, and subsequently licensed to Neon Records in Australia and Disco:wax in the United States. Tobtok also released an accompanying music video. Although the Jonas Blue version released shortly after was far more successful, Tobtok's version also charted in a number of charts, notably Australia, where it received significant airplay (some stations like 2Day FM played it over the Jonas Blue version) and reached number 19 on the ARIA Singles Chart in January 2016, while Jonas Blue's version was at number two. The Tobtok version also charted in the Norwegian VG-lista, Irish IRMA, and Danish Tracklisten charts.

sections.heading: Background and inspiration
sections.wikitext:
In an interview with [[iHeartRadio]], Blue stated Chapman's original 1988 hit is a favorite of his mother, who would often play it in the car. "It was a good song in London [during] that time when I was growing up, so it was always on the radio," he went on to say. "And it just kind of stuck with me. It was that song on the long journeys, and I loved it."<ref name="iHeartRadio">{{Cite web |last=Mastrogiannis |first=Nicole |date=March 24, 2016 |title=INTERVIEW: Who Is Jonas Blue? Everything You Need to Know |url=http://www.iheart.com/news/interview-who-is-jonas-blue-everything-14526661/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160802000741/http://www.iheart.com/news/interview-who-is-jonas-blue-everything-14526661/ |archive-date=August 2, 2016 |access-date=July 11, 2016 |publisher=[[iHeartRadio]]}}</ref>

Regarding Dakota, who provides vocals on the song, Blue said, "... she [said], 'Oh, I've never done dance music before or anything like that so, I'm not kind of sure.' And I was like, 'Listen, you'd be great.' And she came the next day to record it, and what you hear on the radio is her coming in the next day after her show to record it."<ref name="iHeartRadio" /> Blue also admitted that he wanted to create a Swedish-esque sound on the record: "I think with things like the synth lead lines in it, giving it that second hook, I was kind of going for a very kind of Swedish-y kind of sound. That's kind of the influence behind that kind of lead synth line, and that was something which I don't think people have picked up on yet, but they just like the song because of what it is."<ref name="iHeartRadio" />

It was that song on the long journeys, and I loved it."

Regarding Dakota, who provides vocals on the song, Blue said, "... she [said], 'Oh, I've never done dance music before or anything like that so, I'm not kind of sure.' And I was like, 'Listen, you'd be great.' And she came the next day to record it, and what you hear on the radio is her coming in the next day after her show to record it." Blue also admitted that he wanted to create a Swedish-esque sound on the record: "I think with things like the synth lead lines in it, giving it that second hook, I was kind of going for a very kind of Swedish-y kind of sound. That's kind of the influence behind that kind of lead synth line, and that was something which I don't think people have picked up on yet, but they just like the song because of what it is."

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
The Jonas Blue version peaked at number two on the [[UK Singles Chart]], behind [[Zayn Malik]]'s "[[Pillowtalk]]".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gibsone |first=Harriet |date=February 5, 2016 |title=Zayn Malik's debut solo single Pillowtalk goes straight to No 1 |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2016/feb/05/zayn-malik-pillowtalk-goes-straight-to-no-1-uk-singles-chart |access-date=February 8, 2016}}</ref> Its UK peak meant it charted higher than Chapman's original, which peaked at number five on the chart in May 1988 and a position higher upon a re-release in April 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Myers |first=Justin |date=April 20, 2018 |title=12 cover versions that charted higher than the originals |url=http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/its-a-cover-up-12-cover-versions-that-charted-higher-than-the-originals__6580/ |access-date=April 20, 2018 |publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]}}</ref>

Outside the United Kingdom, the Jonas Blue version reached number one in Australia<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ryan |first=Gavin |date=January 30, 2016 |title=ARIA Singles: Jonas Blue 'Fast Car' Is Australia's No 1 |url=http://www.noise11.com/news/aria-singles-jonas-blue-fast-car-is-australias-no-1-song-20160130 |access-date=January 30, 2016 |publisher=Noise11}}</ref> and Hungary, while peaking within the top ten in Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Belgium, New Zealand, and Sweden. In the United States, the Jonas Blue version went to number one on [[Dance Club Songs]].

It reached one billion streams on [[Spotify]] in late February 2023.<ref>{{Citation |title=Fast Car |date=December 4, 2015 |url=https://open.spotify.com/album/55zQqrjWsFHRcI1mxlQSsZ |access-date=February 22, 2023 |language=en}}</ref>
sections.text:
The Jonas Blue version peaked at number two on the UK Singles Chart, behind Zayn Malik's "Pillowtalk". Its UK peak meant it charted higher than Chapman's original, which peaked at number five on the chart in May 1988 and a position higher upon a re-release in April 2011.

Outside the United Kingdom, the Jonas Blue version reached number one in Australia and Hungary, while peaking within the top ten in Germany, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Belgium, New Zealand, and Sweden. In the United States, the Jonas Blue version went to number one on Dance Club Songs.

It reached one billion streams on Spotify in late February 2023.

The song reached number one on the Country Airplay chart in July 2023, making Chapman the first black woman to score a country number one with a solo composition. Additionally, it became the first cover of a pop single to top a Billboard chart based on country radio airplay since Blake Shelton's version of Michael Bublé's 2005 single "Home" reached number one in 2008. On the Country Airplay chart dated September 9, 2023, it held the number two position behind Combs' own "Love You Anyway" at the top, making it the first time in that chart's history that the top two positions were simultaneously occupied by the same artist with no accompanying performers, and only the second time that such a distinction has been achieved by any act overall (with or without accompanying performers).

sections.wikitext:
<!-- See [[WP:COVERSONGS]] for standards for listing cover songs in articles -->
* The initial version of the song "[[Dreams (Gabrielle song)|Dreams]]" by [[Gabrielle (singer)|Gabrielle]] was based around a sample of "Fast Car", but this was removed from the final version because the sample could not be cleared.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Burcher |first1=Nick |title=Paid, Owned, Earned: Maximising Marketing Returns in a Socially Connected World |date=March 3, 2012 |publisher=Kogan Page Publishers |isbn=978-0-7494-6563-6 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QQnp-duPmbMC&pg=PA133 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20231221-fast-car-why-a-35-year-old-folk-anthem-became-one-of-the-songs-of-2023|title=Tracy Chapman and Luke Combs: Why Fast Car became a viral moment at the Grammys|date=February 5, 2024|website=www.bbc.com}}</ref>
*American musician [[Jim O'Rourke (musician)|Jim O'Rourke]] performed a 33-minute long rendition of "Fast Car" in [[Tokyo]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chu |first=Hau |date=April 3, 2021 |title=Perspective {{!}} Tracy Chapman's 'Fast Car' is a beautiful ballad. This 33-minute cover version takes it to a whole new place. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/music/fast-car-cover-song-jim-orourke/2021/04/01/a320a10c-8cbf-11eb-a730-1b4ed9656258_story.html |access-date=February 5, 2024 |newspaper=Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/2017-in-review/a-few-minutes-of-great-pop-song-moments-from-2017|title=A Few Minutes of Great Pop-Song Moments from 2017|first=Hua|last=Hsu|date=December 22, 2017|via=www.newyorker.com}}</reF>
*American [[experimental rock]] band [[Xiu Xiu]] performed a cover of "Fast Car" with some altered lyrics on their 2003 album ''[[A Promise (Xiu Xiu album)|A Promise]]'', with singer [[Jamie Stewart (American musician)|Jamie Stewart]] calling it "hugely, hugely, tremendously influential on our songwriting".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/luke-combs-fast-car-tracy-chapman-top-10-five-burning-questions-1235334697/|title=With So Few Hit Covers in 2023, Why Is Luke Combs’ ‘Fast Car’ Doing So Well?|first=Katie Atkinson,Jason Lipshutz,Melinda Newman,Jessica Nicholson,Andrew|last=Unterberger|date=May 23, 2023}}</reF><ref name="NYT">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/03/16/arts/music/dancing-away-from-the-bleak-life-with-fast-car.html|title=Dancing Away From the Bleak Life With ‘Fast Car’}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://americansongwriter.com/5-experimental-covers-of-hit-songs-that-are-arguably-better-than-the-originals/|title=5 Experimental Covers of Hit Songs That Are (Arguably) Better Than the Originals|first=Em|last=Casalena|date=August 24, 2024}}</reF><reF>[https://pitchfork.com/features/interview/5905-xiu-xiu/ Xiu Xiu | Pitchfork]</reF>
*American band [[Boyce Avenue]] covered the song in 2010, with the YouTube video reaching over 86 million views.<ref name="FCC"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/tracy-chapman-is-making-bank-off-of-luke-combs-fast-car-cover/|title=Tracy Chapman Is Making Bank Off Inferior ‘Fast Car’ Covers|first=Laura Bradley Senior Entertainment|last=Reporter|date=July 6, 2023|website=The Daily Beast}}</reF>
*Several musicians have covered the song during performances on [[BBC Radio 1]]'s In the Live Lounge: Canadian musician [[Justin Bieber]], as well as British musician [[Sam Smith]] in 2016, and American singer [[Khalid (singer)|Khalid]] in 2018.<ref name="FCC">{{Cite web|url=https://people.com/singers-who-covered-tracy-chapman-fast-car-8559631|title=Luke Combs, Justin Bieber and Other Musicians Who Have Covered Tracy Chapman's 'Fast Car'|website=People.com}}</ref><ref name="NYT"/><reF name="FCC2">{{Cite web|url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/tracy-chapman-fast-car-luke-combs/|title='Fast Car': The Long, Distinctive Journey of Tracy Chapman's Hit|date=July 19, 2023|website=Ultimate Classic Rock}}</reF>
*British musician [[Passenger (singer)|Passenger]] covered the song in 2017.<ref name="FCC"/><reF name="FCC2"/>
*American band [[Black Pumas]] performed the song live on ''[[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert]]'' in 2020, and a studio version was included in the deluxe reissue of their [[Black Pumas (album)|self-titled debut album]].<ref name="FCC"/><reF name="FCC2"/>
*American band [[!!!]] covered the song in 2021, speeding it up significantly, with frontman [[Nic Offer]] saying "The goal was to make ‘Fast Car’ sound even faster... Something you would play in a fast fucking car."<reF name="FCC2"/>
sections.text:
* The initial version of the song "Dreams" by Gabrielle was based around a sample of "Fast Car", but this was removed from the final version because the sample could not be cleared.
*American musician Jim O'Rourke performed a 33-minute long rendition of "Fast Car" in Tokyo in 2002.<reF name="FCC2">{{Cite web|url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/tracy-chapman-fast-car-luke-combs/|title='Fast Car': The Long, Distinctive Journey of Tracy Chapman's Hit|date=July 19, 2023|website=Ultimate Classic Rock}}</reF>
*British musician Passenger covered the song in 2017.<reF name="FCC2"/>
*American band Black Pumas performed the song live on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert in 2020, and a studio version was included in the deluxe reissue of their self-titled debut album.<reF name="FCC2"/>
*American band !!! covered the song in 2021, speeding it up significantly, with frontman Nic Offer saying "The goal was to make ‘Fast Car’ sound even faster... Something you would play in a fast fucking car."<reF name="FCC2"/>
